chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Rubberlegs Williams and Johnny Hodges; the Bessie Smith songs date
summary: Willard asks about the Continental date; Young describes Rubberlegs Williams's behavior and the Bessie Smith songs recorded.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: there was a recording on the Continental label with
Yeah, Clyde Hart (inaudible) you and Dizzy and Charlie Parker, Don Byas --
mike Ryan Specs Powell and Rubberlegs Williams, (inaudible)
Oh, have you ever heard that?
I heard the a vocal album.
If you get a chance, please try to hear it. I'll tell you a story on this particular date.

Rubberlegs was a big sissy, you know, great big guy, man, about 6'4"; he weighed about 240. And he loved Johnny Hodges, so he used to walk up to Johnny Hodges and -- let me feel it, man; he'd grab down there and grab that Johnny Hodges' penis, you know.

So Johnny, he say, I can't beat him. I just let him go feel it, he says, and then he go on. All right, he says, but you can't resist the guy, so big and strong. So he loved Johnny's playing, man. He just thought the world of -- anybody bother Johnny, he probably would have killed him.
So anyway, this particular day we were making those records. We were doing -- I remember this so well, we were
doing some of Bessie Smith's songs and -- for him. He was singing them -- 'What's the Matter Now, you been a good old rag, and she done broke down and some of these things. You got those listed?
I got -- yeah, 'What's the Matter Now, 'I want every bit of it'--
